title: Pre-reset session regains protected access after password recovery completes in another session
environment: Live UAT; two independent Chromium sessions; disposable QA CASE_VIEW user
preconditions: Create a new synthetic user and own case; complete initial password change
Preserve session A without exporting its cookie
steps: Sign in to disposable user in session A and read own QA case
As QA administrator reset that disposable user password to a new temporary password
Read case through A:403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED confirms reset took effect
Open independent session B; sign in using the new temporary password; complete forced password change
Use original A, without logging in again or supplying the new password, to GET the owned case and open its browser detail page
expected: Security recovery should invalidate pre-reset sessions; old session should not regain protected access after another session completes recovery
actual: Original session A resumes protected case access with HTTP200 after B completes recovery; reproduced independently in API suite and browser form suite
contract_note: Current Phase2 acceptance specifies forced change and audit, but does not explicitly require session revocation. The403 during forced change passes current contract. This finding is a demonstrated recovery-security weakness and missing acceptance criterion, not an asserted violation of an explicit existing401 requirement.
impact: A holder of a previously compromised session can regain access after the legitimate user completes an administrative password recovery, without knowing the reset/new password.
fix_guidance: Implementation fix independently verified on the stated UAT SHA; do not request repeated implementation. Reopen only with fresh regression evidence.
uat_policy: Security remediation requested before full acceptance; no public-release approval. No deployment or infrastructure modification by QA.
